test-expungement-parity-delta-mutations..reason: Proves the reviewed screening-parity delta mechanism is a constraint rather than a bypass: 11 mutations - a second added question, a reworded existing question, reordered existing questions, the approved question moved to another stage, another jurisdiction, another pathway, a path prefix widening, byte drift in an approved file, an unrecognised schema key, an absent record and a malformed record - each turn verify-expungement-plain-language-values red, and each is checked for the right failure message rather than only a non-zero exit.

test-rcap-consumer-payment-http-mutation.reason: Proves the P1-P18 suite is load-bearing: 7 mutations, each removing one guarantee, all turn it red. Two further guarantees are named in the harness as intentionally unmutated because the application layer is not their only defence.

test-rcap-image-fingerprint-mutations.mj.reason: Blocking via verify-rcap-worker-publication-workflow.mjs, which spawns it and fails if it fails; kept out of the npm test chain string because package.json is an image input. 11 mutations - file drift, missing input, src/ and scripts/lib/ working-tree change, omitted fingerprint key, silent algorithm change, checkpoint tree substitution, stale base, rewritten hash, hand edit, waived equivalence - each turns verify-rcap-image-input-fingerprint red for its named reason, with signal-safe byte restoration.

test-rcap-phase54-mutations.mjs.reason: Proves each Phase 54 defence is load-bearing: 5 mutations — phase omitted, RLS not enabled, browser-role revokes dropped, reserved slug claimable, shape constraint stops discriminating — all turn the namespace proof red.

verify-expungement-consumer-payment-http.reason: The application-to-job boundary proof: P1-P18 driven through the real webhook and consumer render routes, with signatures produced by the Stripe SDK and migrations 26-53 applied to an ephemeral cluster. It is the only coverage that executes the raw-body/signature wiring rather than grepping for it.

verify-f1-evidence-markers.mjs.reason: F1-R evidence-hardening tool: proves a run's marked log block and its evidence artifact say the same thing, re-deriving totals from per-case results. Takes a run log as input, so it runs against each F1 run's output (and via --self-test), not in the repository chain.

verify-rcap-component-deferral-runtime.m.reason: The captain-owned runtime proof for the ten dependency-bearing composed routes: all 31 component treatments resolve, English and Spanish are complete and genuinely distinct, every participant claim cites a resolving evidence carrier, payment and checkout stay closed, no packet or partner credit is consumed, no render job is built, and the Briefcase handoff is present. Includes --mutations, which requires ten deliberate breakages — among them making the deferred route sellable in the resolver and removing either engine adapter's clamp — to come back red. Wired by the captain in window 2026-08-12-w3. It proves runtime behaviour only; it promotes nothing.

verify-rcap-consumer-person-namespace.mj.reason: Proves the fourteen properties the reserved consumer person namespace depends on, against a real cluster carrying 26-54. N1-N8 cover namespace behaviour; R1-R6 cover the role, tenant, reporting, entitlement, attribution and isolation dimensions Phase 54 enforces in the database. R6 is a positive control: the sanctioned server-side path still resolves consumer persons after the lockdown.
verify-rcap-consumer-person-namespace.mj.closedByPhase54: rcap_persons now has RLS enabled, a service_role-only policy, no anon or authenticated grants, a trigger refusing the reserved slug on partner_records, and a two-way namespace shape constraint.

verify-rcap-image-input-fingerprint.mjs.reason: Blocking via verify-rcap-worker-publication-workflow.mjs, which spawns it and fails if it fails. verify-tracked-mutation-safety.mjs.reason: Proof that an interrupted mutation harness cannot strand tracked bytes. Every case kills a real child process mid-mutation and hashes what is left on disk: SIGTERM against application source and against two migrations, SIGHUP, an uncaught exception, and SIGKILL — which is expected to strand the mutation, because no process can catch it, and which then proves the journal recovery puts the file back. Also proves a second mutator is refused by name, a tree-reading guard refuses to read a tree mid-mutation, and the Phase 52 and 54 suites still report every mutation red under the guard. Runs first in the chain so a stranded journal is recovered before anything else reads the tree.
